## Summary

I successfully fixed the GitHub issue #46 which reported that `GET /api/todos/` was returning 404 instead of 400 for empty ID parameters.

### Root Cause
The routing logic was filtering out empty strings from URL path segments, causing trailing slashes to be silently dropped. This meant:
- `/api/todos` would route correctly to list todos (200)
- `/api/todos/` would also route to list todos (200) instead of treating the empty segment as an invalid ID parameter

### Changes Made

1. **`/workspace/todo-api/api/handler.js`** (line 110-114)
   - Changed slug normalization to NOT filter empty strings from the split path
   - Before: `.split('/').filter(Boolean)` 
   - After: `.split('/')`
   - This ensures `/api/todos/` becomes `['todos', '']`, properly routing to `handleTodoById` which validates and rejects empty IDs with 400

2. **`/workspace/todo-api/dev-server.js`** (line 101)
   - Updated local dev server to match the handler's slug processing
   - Before: `.split('/').filter(Boolean)`
   - After: `.split('/')`
   - Ensures dev-server and production Vercel runtime have consistent behavior

3. **`/workspace/todo-api/test/handler.test.js`** (added test)
   - Added test case `GET /api/todos/ with empty id returns 400` to prevent regression
   - Verifies the fix works correctly

### Testing
- All 10 tests pass (9 existing + 1 new)
- Verified edge cases:
  - `/api/todos` → 200 (list todos) ✓
  - `/api/todos/` → 400 (invalid empty ID) ✓
  - `/api/todos/search` → 200 (search endpoint) ✓
  - Valid numeric IDs preserve existing behavior ✓

The fix now ensures the API contract matches the OpenAPI specification which defines `/api/todos/{id}` as requiring a valid integer parameter, returning 400 for invalid IDs.
